title: Mainland Mandarin
about: For someone who already reads and speaks Chinese well, but whose Mandarin is Malaysian. Three layers: habits to swap, the moves that keep any conversation going, and themes with the words mainland speakers actually use.

habits.note: 有 + verb as a past marker is Malaysian / southern. In the mainland, drop 有 and use 过 or 了.
Same habit: 有 + verb in a question. Use 了 + 吗, or 吃了没？
先 after the verb comes from Cantonese. In standard Mandarin 先 goes before the verb.
Comparisons use 比: A 比 B + adjective.

habits.en: I got told off by the boss.
habits.note: Passive with 被 (plus 了). 给 is heard in casual northern speech, but 被 is the safe choice.
讲 sounds southern. 说 is the everyday verb for 'say' and 'speak'.
几时 is Cantonese / literary. Say 什么时候.
几多 is Cantonese. Say 多少.
做么 comes from Cantonese 做咩. Use 怎么 (how come) or 为什么. For a past event, 没 not 不.
酱 is a Malaysian contraction of 这样. Say 这样 or 这么.
lah / loh / meh have no mainland equivalent. Use 真 / 太…了 / 挺…的, and particles 啊, 吧, 呢.
行 and 没问题 are the mainland 'OK'. 好的 and 好嘞 too.
粒 is for small grains (一粒米). Apples, eggs, oranges take 个.
Swap English words for Chinese ones. 很牛 is the casual version.

habits.en: I have to work overtime today.
habits.note: OT → 加班.

habits.py: Xià ge xīngqī wǒ qù chūchāi.
habits.en: I'm on a work trip next week.
habits.note: outstation → 出差.
free → 有空.
WhatsApp is not used in China; everything is WeChat. 微信 works as a verb.
cincai → 马虎 (careless) or 随便 (whatever, anything goes).
sian (Hokkien) → 无聊 (bored) or 烦 (fed up), 没劲 (no fun).
confirm → 确定. 'Confirm a booking' → 确认.
cancel → 取消.
jam → 堵 / 堵车. 塞车 is understood but sounds southern.
lepak → 坐坐, 玩玩, 聚一聚.

chunks.note: A standard opener in China. People answer with a province or city.

chunks.en: What have you been up to?

chunks.note: A greeting, not an invitation. More common with older people.
What a host says. Repeating the verb sounds warm.

chunks.zh: 我们那边也说中文，不过口音不太一样。
chunks.py: Wǒmen nàbiān yě shuō Zhōngwén, búguò kǒuyīn bú tài yíyàng.
chunks.en: We speak Chinese back home too, but the accent's different.

chunks.zh: 我中文还可以，就是有些词不太熟。
chunks.py: Wǒ Zhōngwén hái kěyǐ, jiùshì yǒuxiē cí bú tài shú.
chunks.en: My Chinese is OK, there are just some words I'm not used to.

chunks.py: Nǎlǐ nǎlǐ, hái chà de yuǎn ne.
chunks.en: Not at all, I've a long way to go.
chunks.note: The modest reply when someone says 你中文说得真好. 过奖了 works too.
我是做……的 = I work in … The usual way to say your job.

chunks.en: I'm here on a work trip.

chunks.py: Wǒ shì dì-yī cì lái Zhōngguó.
chunks.en: It's my first time in China.

chunks.py: Nǐ shì zuò shénme gōngzuò de?

chunks.note: Literally 'real or fake?'. Very common, friendly.

chunks.py: Nǐ píngshí zhōumò dōu gàn má?
chunks.en: What do you usually do at weekends?
How do you say this in Chinese?
Oh, so that's how it is.

chunks.note: 挺……的 = quite …. Very mainland, softer than 很.
Buys you time while you find the word.
倒 softly introduces a different view.

chunks.py: Máfan nǐ bāng wǒ pāi zhāng zhào.
chunks.en: Could you take a photo for me?

chunks.note: The all-purpose polite opener. More common than 对不起 for small things.

chunks.en: Could you do it a bit cheaper?

chunks.py: Nǐ néng shuō màn yìdiǎnr ma?
chunks.en: Could you speak a bit slower?

chunks.zh: 我没听懂，能再说一遍吗？
chunks.py: Wǒ méi tīngdǒng, néng zài shuō yí biàn ma?
chunks.en: I didn't catch that, could you say it again?

chunks.note: To drivers, delivery people, colleagues, anyone who's done something for you.

chunks.en: Thanks, sorry to put you out.

chunks.note: Cheerful. Service staff and drivers say it all the time.

chunks.en: You're welcome / don't stand on ceremony.

chunks.py: Gǎitiān yìqǐ chī ge fàn ba.

chunks.en: Let's add each other on WeChat.

chunks.note: One person shows their WeChat QR code, the other scans.
The host says this to a guest who's leaving.

themes.title: Getting around
themes.intro: Taxis are ordered on an app, trains are fast, and everyone has a map app. Drivers are 师傅.

swaps.note: To take one: 打车. Ride-hailing app: 滴滴.
Often just 公交. A long-distance coach is 大巴.
City streets are full of 电动车 (electric scooters).

dialogue.zh: 去哪儿？
dialogue.en: Where to?

dialogue.zh: 师傅，去火车南站，谢谢。
dialogue.en: To the South railway station, please.

dialogue.zh: 好嘞。赶时间吗？
dialogue.en: Right. In a hurry?

dialogue.zh: 有点儿。大概要多久？
dialogue.en: A bit. Roughly how long?

dialogue.zh: 现在是高峰期，有点儿堵，得四十分钟吧。
dialogue.en: It's rush hour and a bit jammed, about forty minutes.

dialogue.zh: 行，那您看着走吧。
dialogue.en: OK, take whichever way you think best.

dialogue.zh: 到了。前面不能停，我靠边放你下来。
dialogue.en: Here we are. Can't stop in front, I'll pull over.

dialogue.zh: 没问题。我扫码付吧。辛苦了，师傅！
dialogue.en: No problem. I'll pay by QR code. Thanks!

dialogue.zh: 好，慢走啊！
dialogue.en: OK, take care!

themes.title: Paying & phones
themes.intro: Almost everything is paid by scanning a QR code with WeChat Pay or Alipay. Cash works but is rare.

swaps.note: Messages, calls, payments and mini-apps all live in WeChat.

swaps.en: the unit of money in speech
swaps.note: Prices are said in 块 and 毛: 三十八块五 = ¥38.50. Written: 元.

swaps.cn: 淘宝 / 京东 / 拼多多

dialogue.zh: 一共三十八块五。
dialogue.en: That's 38.50 altogether.

dialogue.zh: 可以扫码吗？
dialogue.en: Can I pay by QR code?

dialogue.zh: 可以，扫这个就行，微信、支付宝都可以。
dialogue.en: Yes, scan this one, WeChat or Alipay are both fine.

dialogue.zh: 好的……付了，你看一下。
dialogue.en: OK… paid, have a look.

dialogue.zh: 收到了。要袋子吗？
dialogue.en: Got it. Do you want a bag?

dialogue.zh: 不用了，谢谢。对了，这儿能借充电宝吗？
dialogue.en: No thanks. By the way, can I rent a power bank here?

dialogue.zh: 门口那儿有，扫码就能借。
dialogue.en: There's one by the door, just scan to borrow.

dialogue.zh: 好嘞，谢谢啊。
dialogue.en: Great, thanks.

themes.title: Eating out
themes.intro: You often order by scanning a code on the table. Call staff 服务员 (or 老板 in a small place). The bill is 买单.

swaps.note: 埋单 is the Cantonese writing. In the mainland you'll see 买单, and hear 结账 more in the north.

dialogue.zh: 几位？
dialogue.en: How many?

dialogue.zh: 两位。有菜单吗？
dialogue.en: Two. Is there a menu?

dialogue.zh: 扫桌上的码点菜就行。
dialogue.en: Just scan the code on the table to order.

dialogue.zh: 好。你们的招牌菜是什么？
dialogue.en: OK. What's your signature dish?

dialogue.zh: 水煮鱼和宫保鸡丁，点的人最多。
dialogue.en: Poached fish in chilli and kung pao chicken, they're the most popular.

dialogue.zh: 那来一个水煮鱼，要微辣，不要香菜。
dialogue.en: Then one poached fish, mildly spicy, no coriander.

dialogue.zh: 好的，还要别的吗？
dialogue.en: Sure, anything else?

dialogue.zh: 先这样吧，不够再点。
dialogue.en: That's it for now, we'll order more if we need.

dialogue.zh: 服务员，买单！剩下的帮我们打包一下。
dialogue.en: The bill please! And could you pack up the leftovers?

themes.title: Work talk
themes.intro: Small talk about work is everywhere. Your manager is 领导, and long hours have a whole vocabulary.

swaps.note: 老板 is the owner; 领导 is whoever is above you.

vocab.en: go to work / be at work

vocab.note: Often just 卷: 太卷了.

dialogue.zh: 你今天几点下班？
dialogue.en: What time do you finish today?

dialogue.zh: 本来六点，但领导临时要开会，估计又得加班了。
dialogue.en: Six in theory, but the boss called a meeting, so probably overtime again.

dialogue.zh: 哎呀，太卷了。
dialogue.en: Ugh, it's such a rat race.

dialogue.zh: 可不是嘛。你们部门呢？
dialogue.en: Tell me about it. What about your department?

dialogue.zh: 我们还好，不怎么加班，就是工资一般般。
dialogue.en: We're OK, not much overtime, the pay's just so-so.

dialogue.zh: 那也挺好的，至少有时间陪家人。
dialogue.en: That's not bad, at least you have time for family.

dialogue.zh: 是啊。说实话，我最近在考虑跳槽。
dialogue.en: True. Honestly, I've been thinking about changing jobs.

dialogue.zh: 真的假的？那你想去哪儿？
dialogue.en: Seriously? Where would you go?

dialogue.zh: 还没想好，看情况吧。
dialogue.en: Haven't decided, we'll see.

themes.title: Home & daily life
themes.intro: Flats are in a 小区 (gated estate) run by 物业. Parcels go to lockers, and everything can be delivered.

vocab.en: one month's deposit, three months up front

dialogue.zh: 房子看得怎么样？
dialogue.en: So, what do you think of the flat?

dialogue.zh: 挺好的，就是空调好像有点儿问题。
dialogue.en: It's nice, but the air-con seems to have a problem.

dialogue.zh: 没事儿，我明天找人来修。
dialogue.en: No problem, I'll get someone to fix it tomorrow.

dialogue.zh: 好的，麻烦您了。房租怎么付？
dialogue.en: Great, thanks. How do I pay the rent?

dialogue.zh: 押一付三，每个月五号前转账给我就行。
dialogue.en: One month's deposit and three months up front, then transfer to me before the 5th.

dialogue.zh: 物业费包括在里面吗？
dialogue.en: Is the management fee included?

dialogue.zh: 不包括，物业费另外交。
dialogue.en: No, that's paid separately.

dialogue.zh: 明白了。快递一般放哪儿？
dialogue.en: I see. Where do parcels usually go?

dialogue.zh: 小区门口有快递柜，扫码取。
dialogue.en: There are lockers at the estate gate, scan to collect.

dialogue.zh: 行，那就定了吧。
dialogue.en: OK, let's go ahead then.

themes.title: Meeting people
themes.intro: Being Malaysian Chinese is a great conversation starter. Expect questions about your Chinese and your languages.

swaps.note: Mainlanders call it 闽南话. 福建话 can mean any of Fujian's many dialects.
Both are understood; 粤语 is the formal name.
华语 is the Southeast Asian name. In China: 普通话 (spoken), 中文 (the language generally).

vocab.en: mix in (夹英文 = throw in English)

dialogue.zh: 听你口音，不像本地人啊。
dialogue.en: From your accent, you're not local, are you?

dialogue.zh: 对，我是马来西亚华人。
dialogue.en: Right, I'm Malaysian Chinese.

dialogue.zh: 真的啊？怪不得！那你们那边都说中文吗？
dialogue.en: Really? No wonder! So does everyone speak Chinese there?

dialogue.zh: 华人基本上都会说，不过平时也说闽南话、粤语，还会夹很多英文和马来文。
dialogue.en: Most Chinese do, but we also speak Hokkien and Cantonese, and mix in lots of English and Malay.

dialogue.zh: 挺有意思的。那你来这边习惯吗？
dialogue.en: Interesting. Have you got used to it here?

dialogue.zh: 还行吧，就是有些说法不太一样。比如我们说“德士”，你们说“出租车”。
dialogue.en: Pretty much, just some expressions are different. We say 'teksi', you say 出租车.

dialogue.zh: 哈哈，原来是这样。你中文说得真好！
dialogue.en: Ha, I see. Your Chinese is really good!

dialogue.zh: 哪里哪里，还差得远呢。对了，加个微信吧，有空一起吃个饭。
dialogue.en: Not at all. By the way, let's add each other on WeChat, and get a meal sometime.

dialogue.zh: 好啊，我扫你。
dialogue.en: Sure, I'll scan you.
